blocks.title: Dive & Sail with Monik Saab
blocks.lede: A day, a night at anchor, or the Thanksgiving weekend off Espíritu Santo. Monik leads the dives, with all the gear on board. The Eagle Ray crew sails the boat, cooks, and reads the sea. For certified divers. Never dived? Ask us about a first session with Monik.
blocks.imageAlt: Monik Saab, Eagle Ray Expedition Leader, scuba diving in La Paz

blocks.body:
## WHO IS MONIK

Monik grew up on a beach in Brazil. She spent sixteen years in large corporations and teaching English, then made the sea her work.

Today she is a PADI dive instructor and a licensed expedition guide in Mexico, with six years diving Baja California Sur and a license to guide in the Revillagigedo Islands.

Before the first dive, she watches: who is relaxed, who checks their gear twice, who wants to go deeper. Then she plans each dive around them. Which site, how deep, when to get in, and when the best thing is to stay on deck.
blocks.moreText:
More about Monik:

* PADI dive instructor
* SECTUR-certified tour guide (NOM-09)
* Licensed to guide in the Revillagigedo Islands
* STCW and Seaman's Book
* Seasons on yachts with helideck operations
* Has organised multi-day dive trips for her own community
* Dive briefings in English, Spanish, Portuguese or German

Follow her dives and students on Instagram: [@nikdive](https://www.instagram.com/nikdive/)

blocks.title: Three ways to dive with Monik in November
blocks.intro:
All three sail from Marina Palmira, La Paz, on a Beneteau Sense 55 sailboat, with Monik, an Eagle Ray captain and an Eagle Ray chef. Dives and dive gear are included. Pick one, or join two back to back.

Book a suite with a partner or a friend, or take the whole boat with your people.

blocks.bookingInfo:
* 20% deposit to book.
* The balance is due 30 days before departure: October 24 for the Dive Day, October 25 for One Night at Anchor, October 27 for the Thanksgiving expedition. If you book after that date, you pay the full amount when you book.
* If you cancel, the deposit is not refunded.
* If we cancel, because the departure doesn't fill or for safety, you get 100% back.
* Each departure is confirmed once two suites are booked. If not, you get 100% of what you paid back, or a new date.

Want more days, or the whole boat for your own group? Write to us.

blocks.title: What is a day on board with Monik like?
blocks.intro: Each day has a structure, not a schedule. Monik and the captain adjust it to the wind, the visibility and how the group is diving. No one has to do every dive.

steps.stepText: Coffee on deck while the captain takes the boat to the first site.
Monik briefs the group on deck, then you go in.
Lunch cooked on board with local produce, and time to talk about what you saw down there.
On the days with a second dive, Monik takes the group back in. On the others: kayak, paddleboard, a walk on an island beach. Or nothing at all.
Logbooks, the light going down over the desert, the next day's plan.
Dinner on board. If there was a catch that day, it's on the table.

blocks.title: Diving with Monik
blocks.blurb: The last check, the step off the boat, the surface noise gone. Then it's your breath and whatever the sea decides to show you.

photos.alt: Monik witha group of scuba in la paz

blocks.photoNote: Big photo: Monik diving with the group, or divers entering the water
blocks.more:
You wake up at anchor with the site close by. No drive to the marina, no ride back to a hotel. Between dives you sail, swim, eat what the chef has cooked, and talk about what you saw until it's time to go back in.

**Level**

* For certified divers. Monik checks certifications and logbooks before the trip and plans each dive around the group.
* Some sites ask for Advanced Open Water.
* Coming with someone who doesn't dive yet? Tell us before the trip and Monik prepares a first session for them, with a supplement.

**Gear**

* All the dive gear is on board and included. Bring your own if you prefer.

**Dives**

* Dive Day: 1 dive
* One Night at Anchor: 2 dives
* Thanksgiving expedition: 4 dives, plus a 5th if conditions and the group allow

**Safety**

* Always in buddy pairs, never alone in the water.
* Monik in the water with the group, the boat nearby.

**Where**

* In the sites the captain and Monik choose each day: San Rafaelito, Fang Ming, Isla Ballena, Los Islotes, El Bajito, Roca Tintorera, Los Muellecitos.
* We don't promise a specific site: the sea decides first.

**Between dives**

* Snorkeling, swimming, kayak, paddleboard, island walks, and fishing where it is allowed.

blocks.title: Monik doesn’t sail alone,
blocks.blurb: At Eagle Ray, each expedition is led by people who live the sea. Traveling with Monik are a captain, who handles the boat, reads the sea and chooses each anchorage according to the wind, and a chef who cooks with local products.
blocks.note: The team is assigned according to the boat and the dates; we confirm the Eagle Ray team when you make the final pre-booking. So you can start getting familiar, these are some of the captains and chefs we sail with.

questions.question: Do I need to be certified?
questions.answer: Yes, this trip is for certified divers. If you are coming with someone who has never dived, tell us before the trip: Monik can prepare a first session for them, with a supplement.

questions.question: Can I come with someone who doesn't dive?
questions.answer: Yes. They can snorkel, kayak, paddle and enjoy the boat, or try a first dive session with Monik for a supplement.

questions.question: I'm traveling solo. Can I join?
questions.answer: Yes. You can book a suite to yourself. You never share a suite with someone you don't know.

questions.question: How many people will be on board?
questions.answer: Up to 4 guests on the overnight departures, plus Monik, the captain and the chef.

questions.question: Can I join two departures back to back?
questions.answer: Yes, write to us and we'll put them together.

questions.question: Do I need to bring dive gear?
questions.answer: No, all the gear is on board and included. Bring your certification card and logbook. If you have your own mask, computer or wetsuit, you are welcome to bring them.

questions.question: Can I fly after diving?
questions.answer: Yes, with margin. Monik plans the last dive so you have the hours you need before your flight. On the Thanksgiving expedition there is no dive on the last morning.

questions.question: What happens if the weather turns?
questions.answer: The captain decides the route each day with the wind and the sea. If a site isn't diveable, we go to another one or stay in a sheltered anchorage. The priority is the group's safety and getting back to La Paz on time.

questions.question: How much should I tip?
questions.answer: We recommend 10 to 15% of the trip price.

questions.question: How much do I pay to book, and what if I need to cancel?
questions.answer: A 20% deposit books your place, and the balance is due 30 days before departure. If you book later than that, you pay in full. If you cancel, the deposit is not refunded. If we cancel, you get 100% back.

questions.question: Do I need a fishing license?
questions.answer: The Sea of Cortez requires one for every adult on board. It's included.

blocks.title: Good to know before you come

questions.question: Local currency
questions.answer:
Mexican peso (MXN). Bills from $20 to $1,000 MXN; the $500 and $1,000 bills can sometimes be difficult to change in small shops. Hotels and most tourism businesses in La Paz accept cards, but in smaller places you will need cash. There are ATMs all over the city.

You won’t need it on board: meals and non-alcoholic drinks are included.

questions.question: How to get there
questions.answer:
La Paz Airport (LAP) is 20 minutes from the marina, with domestic flights and some routes to the United States.

The transfer from the airport to the marina is included.

Los Cabos Airport is 2 hours away by road and is sometimes more convenient, depending on where you are flying from; if that is your case, write to us and we’ll look into it.

questions.question: Food
questions.answer:
La Paz cuisine revolves around the sea: chocolate clams cooked over hot stones, ceviche with a touch of mayonnaise, marlin or octopus quesadillas, and machaca, dried beef or pork, the classic that does not come from the sea. Fish tacos are an icon of the peninsula (they were born farther north, in Ensenada), but here they are just as much at home.

On board, the chef cooks with what these same waters provide, unless you ask for something else.

questions.question: What to bring
questions.answer:
Tip: bring less than you think.

On board you only need a dry swimsuit to change into; the crew takes care of the rest.

For everything else, light clothing made from natural fabrics for the dry heat, something for the cooler evenings, and a hat, because the desert sun hits directly.

For diving: your certification card and logbook. The rest of the gear is on board.

questions.question: Weather
questions.answer:
Desert climate, dry almost all year round.

November: northerly winds may come in, bringing short choppy seas. That is why the captain decides the route each day.

Winter (December to February): mild, from 18 to 24 °C, the most pleasant season.

Spring (April and May): the heat starts rising.

Summer (June to August): hot and humid, from 28 to 31 °C.

Hurricane season: from May 15 to November 30, with the risk concentrated in August and September.

questions.question: Connection
questions.answer:
At sea, signal is limited, so expect to be disconnected for a good part of the day.

In La Paz, wifi works well. Starlink on board.
